title: Paramount Developing Animated Bollywood Musical 'Diya' With Dungeons & Dragons Producers
excerpt: The mythology-based fantasy adventure reunites the GoldDay production duo with Paramount, marking Hollywood's biggest animated bet on Indian storytelling yet.
body:
• Paramount is developing 'Diya,' an animated Bollywood-focused musical rooted in Indian mythology, with producers Jonathan Goldstein and John Francis Daley through their GoldDay banner.
  • The film is directed by Nitya Mehra (Baar Baar Dekho, Made in Heaven) with Kunal Nayyar of The Big Bang Theory fame executive producing.
  • Originally announced in 2022 with Reel FX Originals, the project has now landed at Paramount under Goldstein and Daley's first-look deal with the studio.
  • Diya is described as a fantasy adventure set in the world of Indian folklore, with a screenplay by Shiwani Srivastava (Wedding Season) and Dr. Amy Bhatt.

Paramount is developing an animated Bollywood-focused musical titled Diya, with Jonathan Goldstein and John Francis Daley — the filmmaking duo behind Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves — producing through their GoldDay production company, according to The Hollywood Reporter.

The project marks one of the most significant investments by a major Hollywood studio in Indian-themed animated storytelling, pairing Paramount's distribution muscle with creative talent rooted in both Bollywood and Indian American filmmaking.

From Indie Origins to Studio Backing

Diya was first announced in June 2022 as a collaboration between Reel FX Originals — the animation company behind The Book of Life — and director Nitya Mehra. The project has since found its way to Paramount through Goldstein and Daley's first-look deal with the studio, struck after the success of their Dungeons & Dragons adaptation.

Mehra, who made her directorial debut with the 2016 Bollywood film Baar Baar Dekho starring Sidharth Malhotra and Katrina Kaif, has since earned acclaim as showrunner and director of Amazon's Made in Heaven. Her career began as an assistant director to Ang Lee on Life of Pi and Mira Nair on The Namesake.

Actor and producer Kunal Nayyar, best known for playing Raj Koothrappali on CBS's The Big Bang Theory, is executive producing through his company, Good Karma Productions. Nayyar has previously voiced characters in the Trolls and Ice Age animated franchises.

A Story Steeped in Indian Mythology

Diya is described as a fantasy adventure set in the world of Indian mythology and folklore. The screenplay is written by Shiwani Srivastava, who penned Netflix's Wedding Season, and Dr. Amy Bhatt. Steve O'Brien and Jared Mass of Reel FX Originals are producing alongside the GoldDay team.

The project draws comparisons to Reel FX's earlier success with The Book of Life, the 2014 animated film directed by Jorge R. Gutiérrez and produced by Guillermo del Toro that brought Mexican mythology and Day of the Dead traditions to global audiences. That film grossed over $100 million worldwide and spawned a Netflix sequel series.

Diya aims to do something similar for Indian folklore — a vast, visually rich tradition that has remained largely untapped by Western animation studios despite India's massive global cultural footprint.

"That film grossed over $100 million worldwide and spawned a Netflix sequel series."

Hollywood's Growing Indian Bet

The project arrives at a time when Hollywood is increasingly looking to Indian stories and talent. Recent years have seen the success of Indian-origin filmmakers and performers across the industry, from Chloé Zhao and Nisha Ganatra to Riz Ahmed and Charithra Chandran.

In animation specifically, the Indian market represents one of the fastest-growing audiences globally, and projects like Diya signal studios' recognition of the commercial potential of culturally specific storytelling — the same logic that drove Pixar's Coco, Disney's Moana, and Encanto.

For Indian Americans, the film carries particular significance. The involvement of Mehra, Nayyar, and screenwriter Srivastava ensures the story is shaped by people with direct cultural connections to the material — a contrast to earlier Hollywood attempts at Indian-themed content that often relied on outsider perspectives.

What to Watch For

No release date or casting details for voice roles have been announced. Goldstein and Daley, who recently established GoldDay as a multi-year production venture with Paramount, are expected to bring the same genre-blending sensibility they applied to Dungeons & Dragons and Game Night.

The project's progression from a smaller animation house to a major studio suggests growing industry confidence in Indian mythology as commercial animated fare — a development that will be watched closely by both Hollywood and Bollywood.
